newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan investors can assess stock risks - minister.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan investors can assess stock risks - minister.

text.p: Taiwan Finance Minister Paul Chiu said on Tuesday that investors should be able to assess their own risk in the rallying stock market and that the market itself should determine share values.

Asked whether the market was overheated after a trading day that saw daily turnover surge to a record T$238.9 billion, Chiu reserved judgment, saying the market was "transparent" and that supply and demand should be what determined share values.
Chiu spoke briefly at Taipei's international airport on returning from an Asia-Pacific finance ministers' meeting in the Philippines, the state-funded Central News Agency reported.

With new investors pouring into the market, stock turnover on Tuesday soared above the record of T$216 billion set on March 16, 1990, when the market was tumbling from its all-time closing high of 12,495.34.
The benchmark index ended down 57.07 points or 0.67 percent at 8,460.63 after a wild roller-coaster session.
Some analysts have cautioned that Taiwan's rally was driven mainly by loose liquidity, saying stocks may have been overbought and that the rises do not trully represent companies' fundamental value.
A dramatic rally that has sent the index 80 percent higher since February 1996 has lured thousands of new investors into the market, pushing turnover ever higher, brokers said.
"From old to young, from students to professionals -- stock investment has become a nationwide sport," said Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang.

A central bank official said the central bank would closely monitor whether the sharp stock rises would have an impact on consumer prices, money rates, foreign exchange rates and the real estate market.
